1. **The idea.** The animation compares buying a home with renting and investing the difference, using US history. A grid of small house icons runs from January 1991 to July 2016, one icon per possible start month. Each icon is either lit or dark. Lit means the buyer was ahead after ten years. Dark means the renter's pile was bigger. The sources named are FHFA, BLS, Freddie Mac and K. R. French (CRSP). The frames are labeled "Illustrative", "US only · history, not a forecast", and later "All $ in dollars of the day".

2. **What changes.** Across the six frames, the lit icons are concentrated in the early start months, at the left and front of the grid. Most of the grid stays dark. Frame 1 labels the darkest region "darkest: January 1991". In frames 4 to 6, a caption appears: "16 start months: $1 ended below $1 · all 16 stay lit". A few extra small markers show up beside the lit block, and the "dollars of the day" note is added. The grid itself barely moves.

3. **What it means.** In most historical start months, the renter who invested the difference ended up with the bigger pile after ten years. Only a small set of start months, mostly early ones, had the buyer ahead. The caption adds that in 16 start months an invested dollar ended below a dollar, and in all 16 the buyer was still ahead. So renting and investing usually won in this data, but not always, and it was weakest in the periods when stocks did badly.

4. **Advice a viewer might take.** The frames give no explicit advice. A viewer might infer that "rent and invest the difference" often wins but isn't guaranteed. They might also infer that buying works as protection when investment returns are poor. The "history, not a forecast" and "Illustrative" labels push against treating this as a prediction.

5. **Source of the conclusion.** The animation did not state any advice. Everything in 4 is my own inference from the lit and dark pattern and the captions. The on-screen text only describes what lit and dark mean, notes the 16 months where $1 ended below $1, and warns that this is history and not a forecast.
